title: Finance-Segway concept system and controlled vocabulary
purpose: One authority for what this repository's terms mean and which values its enumerated fields may take. A vocabulary that is written down but not enforced is a document; tools/verify_controlled_vocabulary.py makes this one a control by checking the repository's own data against it.

conventions.definition_style: ISO 704. Each definition is a substitutable noun phrase: it names the superordinate concept and then the characteristics that delimit this concept from its siblings, so the definition can replace the term in a sentence without loss. Definitions do not open with 'is when', 'is where', or 'refers to', and no definition may depend on the term it defines.
conventions.relations: ISO 25964 and SKOS. 'broader' is the superordinate concept (skos:broader), 'related' is an associative link (skos:related), 'altLabels' are non-preferred designations (skos:altLabel) that must never be used in data.
conventions.homographs: Where one designation names two concepts, ISO 704 requires the designations be distinguished rather than the concepts merged. Such cases are recorded under 'homographs' with the resolution.

concepts.definition: A workbook holding a domain's calculation engines and no subject-specific data, from which every instance in that domain is generated.
concepts.scopeNote: Templates carry driver defaults so the engines can be exercised. Those defaults are not claims about any company.

concepts.definition: A Python module that generates a template deterministically, and which is the sole authority for that template's contents.
concepts.scopeNote: A template edited by hand rather than regenerated breaks semantic parity and fails the build.

concepts.definition: A workbook produced by applying one case manifest's inputs to a template.
A dated, sourced study of one real subject, recorded as a manifest, a frozen source snapshot, and a generated instance.
concepts.scopeNote: Every public case in this repository is external historical evidence. None is a production model output.

concepts.definition: The machine-readable record of a public case's inputs, sources, cover metadata, and refresh history, and the only sanctioned way to set an instance's values.
An immutable, hash-digested record of the observations a case rests on, captured at a stated date.
The recorded chain from a value in a workbook back to the published document that disclosed it.
A per-domain table listing each case's sources with publisher, URL, as-of date, snapshot path, and snapshot digest.
The classification of how a manifest input's value was obtained.
concepts.scopeNote: Recorded per input cell. Determines whether the cell earns real-data coverage credit.

concepts.definition: An input kind whose value is read directly from a disclosed figure without arithmetic.
An input kind whose value is computed from disclosed figures by arithmetic that the manifest states.
concepts.scopeNote: The arithmetic must be stated in the input's notes, so a reader can recompute it.

concepts.definition: An input kind whose value is chosen by the modeller because no disclosure of it exists.
concepts.scopeNote: Earns no real-data coverage credit. The bare designation 'modeler' is a non-preferred variant and must not appear in data.

concepts.definition: A manifest record stating why a cell holds a chosen value rather than a sourced one, and what would ground it.
A driver declaration carrying a basis that names real published data bounding the driver's range.
concepts.scopeNote: Counts toward accounted coverage but never toward real coverage.

concepts.definition: A driver declaration whose basis is empty, so its range rests on nothing published.
concepts.scopeNote: Deliberately earns no coverage credit: a driver without a grounded range is still an ungrounded number in a model.

concepts.definition: The share of a template's candidate input cells that a case fills with observed or derived values.
The share of a template's candidate input cells that a case either fills with sourced values or declares as grounded drivers.
A template cell styled as an input and therefore eligible to receive case data.
concepts.scopeNote: Detected by input-blue font colour, ignoring the alpha channel.

concepts.definition: A calculation written independently of a workbook that recomputes the workbook's result for comparison.
concepts.scopeNote: Independence is the whole point: an oracle that reuses the workbook's formulas verifies nothing.

concepts.definition: A model whose recalculated workbook has been compared against a separate pure-Python computation of the same quantities.
A reference check bound to a named accounting or financial identity that an oracle evaluates on committed cases.
Agreement between a committed template and the output its builder produces, compared on cell values, formulas, and sheet structure.
Agreement between a committed template and its builder's output on formatting, column widths, and styling.
concepts.scopeNote: Recalculating a committed template in place breaks this, because the spreadsheet application rewrites presentation metadata.

concepts.definition: The stage a model has reached on this repository's evidence ladder, from mechanical correctness through to independently challenged production use.
A maturity level at which a model builds reproducibly and its workbook checks pass.
A maturity level at which a model additionally carries sourced public cases, an independent oracle, and recorded outcomes.
A maturity level at which a model additionally satisfies eight machine-checked criteria including human effective challenge.
concepts.scopeNote: No model in this repository has reached M3. Criterion G cannot be satisfied by any agent.

concepts.definition: A maturity level at which a model additionally holds evidence accumulated over time from live production use.
concepts.scopeNote: No artifact in this repository counts toward M4.

concepts.definition: A named person's recorded approval of a model, which no automated process may supply.
Critical review of a model by parties with the competence, influence, and independence to change it.
concepts.scopeNote: The term is used here in the sense established by supervisory model-risk guidance.

concepts.definition: A dated, content-hashed prediction registered before the period it predicts has been reported.
concepts.scopeNote: Distinguished from a retrospective reconstruction, which is authored knowing the answer.

concepts.definition: The unskilled prediction a forecast must beat, frozen at registration from data already in the repository.
The proportional reduction in error a forecast achieves against its naive baseline, positive when the forecast is closer.
concepts.scopeNote: Murphy skill: 1 minus the ratio of forecast error to baseline error.

concepts.definition: The supervisory risk classification assigned to a model, governing how much validation evidence it must carry.
concepts.scopeNote: An ordinal tier scale. Distinct from the consulting catalogue's impact severity scale; see homographs.

concepts.definition: The consequence rating of a consulting capability's failure, on an ordered qualitative scale.
concepts.scopeNote: A severity scale, not a tier scale. See homographs.

concepts.definition: The annualised value of a software business's contracted recurring subscriptions at a point in time.
concepts.scopeNote: A management metric with no fixed definition and no XBRL tag. Never sourceable from a filing's tagged facts.

concepts.definition: The transaction price allocated to contracted goods and services a business has not yet delivered.
concepts.scopeNote: A required disclosure with a fixed definition and an XBRL tag, which is why this repository builds its forward-revenue engine on RPO rather than on ARR.

concepts.definition: The portion of remaining performance obligations a business has already billed and carries on its balance sheet.
concepts.scopeNote: Remaining performance obligations less contract liability is the unbilled portion, which appears on no balance sheet.

concepts.definition: The proportion of a period's opening recurring revenue retained at its close after expansion, contraction, and churn, excluding revenue from customers won in the period.
concepts.scopeNote: Excluding new logos is definitional. Including them inflates the figure in the direction a seller prefers.

concepts.definition: The proportion of a period's opening recurring revenue retained at its close after churn alone, giving no credit for expansion.
concepts.scopeNote: Never exceeds net revenue retention.

concepts.definition: A driver declaration recording that a template line has no counterpart in the subject's real economics, so no disclosure could fill it.
concepts.scopeNote: Distinct from an undisclosed driver, and the distinction matters. An undisclosed driver could be filled if the subject disclosed more. A structural mismatch could not be filled by any disclosure, because the quantity the template asks for does not exist for this subject. Collapsing the two hides a modelling limitation behind a data-availability excuse. Three declarations in this repository were mislabelled 'not_disclosed' until the concept system was worked out.

concepts.definition: A forward projection built from data published after the date it claims to have been made on.
concepts.scopeNote: A defect, not a category of evidence. Named so it can be checked for.

homographs.problem: One field name carries two incompatible scales. Model governance registries record an ordinal tier ('Tier 1'); the consulting capability catalogue records a qualitative severity ('HIGH', 'MODERATE', 'CRITICAL'). A consumer reading risk_tier cannot tell which scale a value is on.
homographs.resolution: The designation 'risk_tier' is reserved for the model risk tier concept. The consulting catalogue's field is renamed 'impact_severity'. ISO 704 requires distinguishing the designations rather than merging the concepts, because the concepts are genuinely different.

input_kind.authority: ANSI/NISO Z39.19 controlled vocabulary; ISO/IEC 11179 permissible values

permitted_values.conventional: A public case exercising a model on a subject behaving within its normal operating range.
permitted_values.adversarial: A public case exercising a model on a subject under stress, chosen so the model's limits are visible.

permitted_values.external_historical_cases: DEPRECATED plural variant of external_historical_case; must not be used in new data.
permitted_values.external_historical_case_visual: A rendered presentation of an external historical case.
permitted_values.agent_tool_draft: A draft produced by an agent tool, not yet a public case.

permitted_values.modeled: A forecast produced by a model rather than by carrying a value forward.

permitted_values.undisclosed_term_driver: A driver standing in for a contractual or structural term no filing discloses.
permitted_values.undisclosed_metric_driver: A driver standing in for an operating metric or descriptive attribute no filing discloses.
permitted_values.scenario_lever: A driver whose value is chosen to define a scenario rather than to describe the subject.
permitted_values.structuring_driver: A driver describing a transaction that was never executed and therefore has no disclosed terms.
permitted_values.generated_metadata: A cell populated automatically from the manifest rather than from any observation.
permitted_values.presentation_convention: A cell carrying a display convention rather than a fact about the subject.
permitted_values.balancing_residual: A driver whose value is determined by a constraint that pins it to disclosed data.
permitted_values.not_disclosed: DEPRECATED. Superseded by undisclosed_term_driver and undisclosed_metric_driver, which say which kind.

deprecated_values.$comment: Values present in committed data that the vocabulary rejects for new use. Listed so the checker can distinguish legacy data from a new mistake, and so the cost of each is visible.

driver_type.not_disclosed: structural_mismatch_driver or undisclosed_metric_driver, chosen per site: a mismatch cannot be filled by any disclosure, an undisclosed attribute could be
